lots.title: Supply of Double Glazed Units and Sheet Glass (DPS)
lots.description: Bristol City Council Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the supply of double-glazed units and sheet glass to the Housing Response Repairs service and bulk orders (joiners shop, Wellington Road). Document is Appendix 1 – Evaluation Criteria; the DPS is evaluated in two stages: (a) a selection-criteria stage (Table A) for admission to the DPS and (b) per-call-off award criteria with price/quality/social-value weightings. Document does not enumerate separate numbered lots; bidders indicate which DPS categories they apply for at question 1.20.
requirements: All bidders must meet the minimum selection criteria in Table A to be admitted to the DPS (§1.1).
The consortium as a whole must achieve the selection criteria; if any member fails a section flagged 'all individual consortium members must pass', the whole consortium fails (§1.3).
Employers Liability insurance not less than £10 million; Public Liability insurance not less than £5 million (Table A Q4.1, Q4.3).
Bidder must agree to be bound by liquidated damages, the Bribery Act 2011, and the Restricted Trade Practices Act 1976 (Table A Q4.5–4.7).
Financial standing must be Low or Medium risk; High risk = Fail (Financial Standing Appraisal scoring table).
Authority generally expects turnover of at least 2× the annual contract value and current ratio of at least 1:1 (Financial Standing Appraisal §1.1 bullets).
All employees attending Bristol City Council sites must hold current CSCS certification or equivalent, including sub-contractors (Table A Q11.1).
Bidder must pay Living Wage Foundation Rate on call-off contracts and reflect it in the Pricing Schedule (Table A Q12.1–12.2).
Bidder must have human/technical resources to comply with GDPR by contract award (Table A Q13.1).
Double-glazed units must comply with BS EN 1279 'Glass in Building – Insulating glass units' and carry a minimum 5-year guarantee (Table A Q14.1.1, Q14.1.3).
Response-repair DGUs must be producible and available for collection within Bristol on the same day (Table A Q14.1.2).
Bulk orders from the Wellington Road joiners shop must be available within 4 working days of order, with telephone pre-notification on 9224654 (Table A Q14.1.6).
Deliveries must not be instalment-split unless specifically requested; all goods must arrive packed and secured with a compliant delivery note (Table A Q14.1.7–14.1.8).
Rejected goods must be collected at supplier risk/expense with replacements within 24 hours (Table A Q14.1.9).
Weekly deliveries to a central location free of charge; weekly order spreadsheet; electronic invoicing (Table A Q14.1.10–14.1.12).
Bidder must accept DPS Agreement terms and conditions without alteration and upload Non-Collusion and Non-Canvassing Certificates (Table A Q15.1–15.3).

evaluation_criteria.summary: Pass/Fail gate: bidders must achieve minimum selection criteria in Table A to be admitted to the DPS. Only information provided in each on-line answer is considered; consortium passes as a whole.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: All bidders must achieve the minimum selection criteria in accordance within Table A below, to be admitted to the DPS.

evaluation_criteria.summary: Financial assessment using profitability, net worth, liquidity, current ratio (generally ≥1:1), and turnover (generally ≥2× annual contract value). Low risk = Pass, Medium Risk = Pass, High Risk = Fail.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: Low risk | Pass; Medium Risk | Pass; High Risk | Fail

evaluation_criteria.summary: For call-offs below £25,000, price is weighted 100%. Lowest lump-sum price receives 100 marks; each competing bid loses marks by the percentage by which it exceeds the lowest price; bids >100% over lowest score zero.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: Weighting Range for call-offs with a value below £25,000 | Price | 100%
evidence_anchor.section_ref: §2 Award Criteria for Call-offs, weighting-range table

evaluation_criteria.summary: For call-offs with a value of £25,000 or above, price is weighted in the range 20%–80% (tailored per call-off), scored via the 'standard differential' method with marks scaled to the weighting.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: Weighting Range for call-offs with a value of £25,000 or above | Price | 20% - 80%
evidence_anchor.section_ref: §2 Award Criteria for Call-offs, weighting-range table

evaluation_criteria.summary: Quality questions scored on a 0–5 matrix (Unacceptable to Excellent). Weighted 0%–60% of overall award. Any Quality score of 0 or 1 allows the Council to exclude the bidder from further consideration.

evidence_anchor.section_ref: §2 Award Criteria for Call-offs, Scoring Matrix

evaluation_criteria.summary: Social Value is weighted at 20% of the overall award. Evaluation approach is set out in a separate appendix. Also acts as the tie-breaker: highest Social Value score wins in the event of a tied total.

evidence_anchor.section_ref: §2 Award Criteria for Call-offs, weighting-range table + Tie Breaker
